factProposals.value: Audit log entries are immutable at the persistence layer: AlveraDbContext.SaveChanges/SaveChangesAsync throws AuditLogImmutableException if any AuditLogEntry is in the Modified or Deleted change-tracker state, regardless of caller or permission. Only insertion is ever permitted.

Audit logs are readable via GET /api/auth/audit-log, gated on the Permission.ViewAuditLog permission (held by Admin and OfficeManager; denied with 403 for every other role). Results are most-recent-first and bounded to at most 500 rows per call.

decisions.statement: Interpreted 'a user attempts to modify an audit log, when they do not have permission, then the action is denied' as an unconditional guarantee rather than a permission-differentiated one: no permission in the system grants audit-log modification, and no API endpoint accepts one, so the denial holds for every role including Admin. This is the strongest form of the stated criterion, not a narrower substitute for it.
decisions.rationale: There is no legitimate business reason for any caller, however privileged, to alter or remove an existing audit entry - granting a 'ManageAuditLog' permission that some role could hold would create exactly the tampering risk the story exists to prevent.

decisions.statement: Enforced immutability at the EF Core SaveChanges layer (a single choke point every write passes through) rather than only at the API/controller layer.
decisions.rationale: A controller-level check only protects callers who go through that specific endpoint; a persistence-layer guard protects the guarantee against any future service, script, or admin tool that might otherwise touch AuditLogEntries directly.

limitations.statement: GET /api/auth/audit-log has no filtering (by date range, event type, or target user) yet - it returns the most recent up-to-500 entries only. Acceptable for this story's scope (prove logging + permission-gated visibility + immutability); a dedicated audit-review UI would need filtering/pagination.
